metric.why: Announced megawatts are the leading indicator for land, power, and equipment demand. The published numbers come almost entirely from commercial research firms; this site links to who publishes them rather than republishing figures it cannot verify.
metric.definition: Capacity in permitting, planned, or under construction per market, the standard unit for comparing data center booms across regions.

reading.body:
Announced megawatts in the construction pipeline are the earliest reliable signal of where AI compute capacity will actually exist, because a data center cannot be built without first clearing permitting and securing power.

The pipeline metric, covering capacity in permitting, planned, or under construction, is the standard unit researchers use to compare development booms across regions. It sits upstream of everything else: before racks are installed, before chips are ordered, before a model can train. A market that shows strong pipeline numbers today is where physical AI infrastructure will concentrate in the years ahead.

The underlying figures come from commercial research firms, not from this source. That matters for how much precision to expect. Published pipeline totals reflect announced intentions, and announcements can be withdrawn, delayed, or revised without notice. The data does not cover utilization, actual power draw, or whether permitted capacity ever reaches operation.

What this metric does not tell the reader is equally important. A large pipeline in a given market says nothing about whether the local grid can absorb the load, only that developers have filed for or begun construction at a certain scale. The gap between announced megawatts and energized megawatts is where grid constraints become visible, and that gap is not captured here.
